text:
kevin: quick proposal to split the "capability port" of the runtime: instead of monolithic inference-service surface, we introduce thin, well-typed adapter ports per capability (generate, embed, rerank). goal: reduce cross-cutting deps and make paydown of tech debt incremental.
marta: sounds good in principle. what does an adapter port look like? gRPC proto? HTTP?
kevin: proto-first gRPC for internal services (strong typing + schema evolution). each adapter is a small shim that translates port -> existing runtime impl. adapters own their api contracts and test suites.
devin: major benefit is we can hand off adapters to different teams for iterative paydown. but we need contract stability guarantees or clients will explode.
soph: propose semantic versioning + compatibility rules: minor bumps allowed for additive fields only; breaking changes require a deprecation header cycle (see deprecate pattern). also require a compatibility test harness that runs in CI for any adapter change.
marta: how do we avoid duplication? currently a lot of shared infra (auth, quota, metrics). if we split adapters we'll duplicate that logic.
kevin: infra cross-cutting bits should be pulled into a shared sidecar library/service: auth-proxy, quota-proxy, telemetry-forwarder. adapters are thin and delegate those concerns to sidecars via standardized headers and a small local RPC.
devin: ops question: more services = more SLO endpoints. how do we keep operational cost manageable?
kevin: two levers: 1) start with logical adapters (run in same process as runtime) and flip to separate deployments only when paydown warrants; 2) reduce SLO surface by grouping adapters under composable deployment units with shared infra SLOs.
soph: testing/CI needs: create an adapter conformance suite that runs against a live compatibility runner. adapters must pass golden-response tests and performance budgets (p99 added latency < 2ms).
marta: migration plan?
kevin: tranche plan: stage 0 = define adapter proto + shared sidecar contracts; stage 1 = implement generate and embed adapters as in-process shims; stage 2 = run pilot deployment for low-traffic tenants as separate services; stage 3 = cutover high-traffic customers; stage 4 = decommission monolith endpoints. each stage gated by metrics.
devin: gating metrics list?
kevin: - adapter.latency.p50/p95/p99; - error.rate.by-tenant; - traffic-divergence.rate (golden vs new); - infra.cost.delta. additionally, have rollback thresholds and automatic throttles.
soph: ownership: infra owns sidecars + routing, runtime team owns monolith + initial adapter shims, and domain teams take over adapters during handoff.
marta: risk: adapter proliferation and poor schema discipline. mitigation: enforce schema registry with automated validators and require design review for new adapters.
devin: curious about tenant isolation: can adapters help with per-tenant customizations?
kevin: yes — adapters can encapsulate tenant-specific transformations behind config, reducing runtime branching. but we must avoid per-tenant forks; prefer config tables + feature flags.
soph: ops note: we need topology diagram and a failure-mode matrix (what happens if sidecar auth dies, or adapter lag spikes). I'll draft that.
kevin: action items: 1) I'll author RFC with proto sketches + tranche plan (ETA Wed). 2) Soph to draft failure-mode matrix + SLO proposal (ETA Fri). 3) Devin to prototype conformance harness and a sample in-process adapter (ETA 2 weeks). 4) Marta to create schema registry proposal + governance (ETA 1 week).
